card.name: Words just before a noun naming a thing
card.fires_on: Small linking or modifier words (such, the, for, back, inal, digital) and an opening parenthesis, where a noun for an object or place is expected next. It appears in mixed drug-label and general web text.

modes.label: Linking word before a noun
modes.description: A small word such as 'such', 'the' or 'for' that comes right before a named thing or title.
modes.example: The tapes contain things<< such>> as television recordings from the 19

modes.label: Parenthesis after a drug name
modes.description: An opening bracket after a product name such as Immune Globulin Intravenous, introducing '(Human)' or '(IGIV)'.
modes.example: hemolysis following Immune Globulin Intravenous<< (>>Human) (IGIV) products:

modes.label: Anatomical adjective before a noun
modes.description: An adjective part-way through an anatomical phrase, before the body-space noun.
modes.example: into three (3) inter<<digital>> spaces of each extremity per study.

card.writes: It slightly favors words like 'canonical', 'jar' and 'wall' and disfavors 'edition' and 'manuscript'.
card.plain: It fires on small words that sit just before a noun, and it lowers the chance that the noun is 'edition' or 'manuscript'.
